title: Baude's wire
description: What Baude's heads and hosts say to each other: one JSON object a line (UTF-8, ending in a newline), each with an op. A line is one of the messages below (x-op: its op; x-kind: request, a head's to a host, its req coming back on the reply; reply; event, a host's unasked; frame, on a mesh link; both, either way). x-since: the wire version an op, entity or field came with (none: 1). x-open: an object whose fields aren't the wire's own (claude's stream-json, a tool's call). x-features: what a host may take that isn't an op of its own (its sessions' programs' control requests, an op's field), by the name a host's ops list it by. x-hosts: hosts that speak only part of the wire, and what they take. baudelib/wire.py reads this as it's imported and builds its message classes from it; the Android app's build makes Kotlin of it.
